title: Find a website destination and interpret contact-request outcomes
goal: Find a declared website destination using local command search, or prepare a contact question and interpret recording and delivery outcomes without inventing authority or retrying uncertain requests. Supplemental internal draft for exact local source only.
prerequisites: Match the exact local-source-preview version and pinned source hashes. Historical guide and ledger revision fields remain historical; current bytes are pinned at this record’s base.
Use a public route where the palette can render. A source-listed route or external destination is not guaranteed available in a guarded preview or real deployment.

For contact, have a question left after documentation or in-product recovery, an intended reply address and a message without passwords, tokens, cloud secrets or customer data. There is no attachment upload.
This record supplements existing website navigation/teaching drafts without replacing them; it does not inventory all header/footer/mobile controls or every destination.
permissions: All fourteen proposed control-family labels and proposed screen labels are documentation labels, not installed runtime bindings or permission grants. Command catalog IDs identify source declarations rather than unique DOM controls.

Internal routing and external-window navigation do not authorize provider/API operations, sign-in, protected access, production actions or integration use. Labels/hints cannot certify security, uptime, pricing or release status.
Contact topic/source and production-access query context are labels, not entitlement or provider authority. Opening contact starts neither a ticket nor AI.
Source-only authoring is not genuine human editorial approval. This draft authorizes no publication, contact submission, email, worker invocation, provider action or database operation.

steps.instruction: On a public website route, use ordinary Cmd+K on Mac or Ctrl+K elsewhere to toggle the command palette.
steps.expectedState: The platform-string-based shortcut toggles local overlay state. No palette is rendered on paths beginning /control, /account or /auth; hiding is not authorization. Opening schedules input focus after 30 milliseconds.

steps.instruction: Type a destination term in Search the site… type, then ↵. Try demo, pricing, handbook or status when there are no matches.
steps.expectedState: Filtering is local over label, hint, category and keywords, ignoring case; substring matches rank ahead of ordered-character matches. Empty query groups Product, Resources, Company and External. No AI or search endpoint receives this query through the component.

steps.instruction: Use ordinary Up/Down or pointer hover to choose a result; use ordinary Enter or click its row to open it. Leave composing shortcuts, Enter, Escape and arrows to the input method.
steps.expectedState: Input and global handlers return early on native composing or legacy keyCode229 without consuming the event. Ordinary selection closes the overlay, then uses router.push internally or window.open with noopener/noreferrer externally. The destination may still require authentication, be unavailable or fail.

steps.instruction: Use ordinary Escape, the Close command palette backdrop button, or the shortcut to close the palette.
steps.expectedState: Closing resets query and highlighted index. Query is not a durable draft. Prior-trigger focus restoration, complete focus containment and actual browser/OSIME/AT behavior are not accepted.

steps.instruction: For a product, account, download, security or press/partner question left after self-service recovery, open /contact. Enter Name and Work email, choose the reason, then describe the step, expected result and error in What went wrong?.
steps.expectedState: Name and email are required with maximum 240 characters; message is required with maximum 8000. Topic defaults to Product question and can be Download help, Security, Support or Press / partners. Exact topic=axiom-production-access prepopulates the product message; it grants no entitlement. Hidden Website honeypot is not a normal customer field.

steps.instruction: Before a deliberate Send →, keep sensitive information out and preserve a private copy if needed. Choose Send once and read the resulting outcome.
steps.expectedState: Client checks trimmed required fields and POSTs /api/contact once per handler invocation. Sending… disables the button while submitting; no server-wide deduplication or exactly-once guarantee follows. This article describes the control and does not authorize an authoring-time submission.

steps.instruction: Treat recording as confirmed only when the client receives accepted:true and a nonempty string referenceId. Keep the displayed reference and read email status separately.
steps.expectedState: Confirmed recording displays the reference and sent, failed or not configured email status. It is not a response-time promise, support entitlement, human review, inbox receipt or completed resolution. Review capabilities opens /product and See plans opens /plans; neither navigation purchases access.

steps.instruction: If HTTP 200 lacks acceptance or a valid reference, or if an error/lost response occurs, keep a private copy and contact support before sending again.
steps.expectedState: The error path preserves the message in volatile component state and gives unconfirmed-recording guidance; reload, closing or navigation may lose it. Failure does not prove no server record/email exists. No automatic resend occurs.

steps.instruction: When using the support email link as a recovery route, open your mail handler and separately decide whether to send your message.
steps.expectedState: Opening mail does not prove a message was sent or received. Do not duplicate a confirmed recorded request just because its email status failed or is not configured.

expectedOutcome: The source-described local palette and contact outcomes are understandable. Only accepted:true plus a nonempty reference confirms the client’s recording acknowledgement; email delivery and eventual resolution remain distinct and no actual request was performed.
limitations: Catalog contains 26 current definitions, not 26 unique pages: both download definitions point to /download. Result count is filtered definitions over catalog size, not integration availability, capacity or health. External declarations were not opened or fetched.
Search is local UI state, not AI assistance or a durable saved query. Arrow navigation is bounded; no wrapping or screen-reader announcement acceptance is promised.

Existing evidence describes 13 synthetic rendered keyboard cases and guarded HTTP delivery/build markers. Those artifacts do not prove actual client execution, live destinations, focus, OSIME, AT, mobile or approved media; no new tests/build/browser/HTTP run was performed for this article.

Contact form labels/live regions and browser field types exist, but Work email does not establish company ownership or enterprise identity; actual keyboard/mobile/AT acceptance remains pending. Hidden honeypot yields neutral HTTP200 accepted:false without creating a lead when populated.

Contact limiter runs before reading the body: existing in-process ten-per-sixty-second sliding window keyed by selected IP header/fallback is not distributed abuse protection. A rate-limit response is not instruction to bypass it.

Server trims/caps fields and validates email; ordinary contact requires a message. Legacy free-review/cloud-health defaults are not extra customer controls here. Message pattern redaction before escaping/storage is not complete PII removal or universal secret detection; never rely on it to submit secrets.

Lead creation and pending CONTACT_RESOLUTION job creation are separate nontransactional creates in this handler, with no idempotency key. Later failure may return 500 after a lead exists; partial storage/job outcomes and duplicate requests remain unqualified.

delivery:sent reflects the internal email request’s successful HTTP response, not inbox delivery. Customer acknowledgement is attempted separately and does not determine delivery; missing mail configuration can still yield confirmed recording.

Queued contact job and accepted response do not establish worker execution, AI funding/admission, truthful agent resolution or human review. Worker retry, financial/provider authority, privacy/retention and real storage/recovery remain open.

Draft/internal/media empty/reviewer and reviewedAt null; supplied actual-clock verifiedAt records source author review only. No customer, media, browser/native/AT, retrieval, security or genuine human editorial acceptance is asserted.
recovery: For no search matches, try suggested terms or close and reopen; keep unrelated application task/action history intact. Palette opening does not execute, retry or reconcile that work.

For unavailable or protected destination, use its normal access/recovery flow; do not treat palette visibility or source catalog membership as permission to bypass restrictions. Guarded preview blocks private/API/form/auth and unsupported requests.

For unconfirmed recording, errors or lost responses, preserve the volatile message privately before navigation and ask support before a deliberate retry; no automatic rerequest or exactly-once promise.
For confirmed reference with failed/not-configured email, keep the reference; email status alone does not justify a duplicate request.
For rate limiting, wait and follow ordinary recovery; do not change IP/source/honeypot values to evade the limit.
For mismatched product version, missing/changed pinned sources or unknown controls, abstain from unsupported instructions and request matching reviewed evidence.
